label: Orindal Records
description: Friendship's early album stretches Dan Wriggins' plainspoken, funny-sad songwriting over synthesizer, pedal steel and Rhodes piano, mixing live and programmed drums. It is patient, homemade-sounding Americana about work, loneliness and friendship, closer to a whisper than a shout.
lineage: Grew out of Wriggins, Gill and Cormier's shared Philadelphia apartment; the twisted, ambient-pedal-steel take on Americana that defines Friendship's later, more widely heard Merge records starts here.

label: Orindal Records
description: Recorded to tape with The Low Anthem's Jeff Prystowsky, Dreamin' trades Friendship's earlier drum machines for a warmer, more organic sound built on acoustic guitars, soft drums and a haunting pedal steel. Dan Wriggins' lyrics sit in the gap between intimacy and loneliness, sung in a plainspoken near-murmur.
lineage: A bridge between Friendship's rougher early records and the fuller Merge albums to come; shares its unhurried, country-inflected hush with labelmates like Lomelda and hemlock.

label: Merge Records
description: Friendship's Merge Records debut is gentle, curious and patient, built around Dan Wriggins' plainspoken baritone and lyrics that reward close listening. It is quietly funny and often devastating, evoking a very particular strand of hushed, country-tinged indie rock.
lineage: Documented by Josh Terry as an album he kept returning to well after its release; represents the point where Friendship's slow-burn Americana reached a wider indie audience via Merge.

label: Merge Records
description: Friendship's second Merge album widens their idea of country music further: shambolic guitars against flute pads, a Motown rhythm section under bleary poetry, and Dan Wriggins' ragged baritone cutting through eleven murky, wry songs. As Josh Terry noted, a song about Jerry Garcia and Betty Ford closes out with a drum solo.
lineage: Continues the slow, twang-inflected songwriting Friendship has refined since 2015, now with more polish and range while staying rooted in the same understated, funny-sad register.

label: Disposable America
description: The Boston trio's self-titled debut sets Will Cashion's deadpan, half-sung vocals over slow, heavy, effects-laden guitar figures. It is a foundational document of the 2010s Boston slowcore-adjacent scene, closer to Duster's hazy drift than to any twang, but decisive for the band's later sound.
lineage: Draws on Duster and Codeine-style slowcore fed through a more melodic, riff-driven Boston indie-rock lens; sets up the run of Run for Cover albums that followed.

label: Run for Cover Records
description: So Divine widens Horse Jumper of Love's palette slightly while keeping their signature slow tempos and heavy-lidded, half-mumbled vocals. Guitars still swell into distorted crescendos, but the songwriting is more direct and melodic than the debut.
lineage: First album for Run for Cover, the label that would house the band through its most acclaimed run; still indebted to Duster/Codeine slowcore.

label: Run for Cover Records
description: Natural Part is a tighter, more focused set of songs than the band's earlier records, still built on Will Cashion's murmured deadpan and slow-burn guitar dynamics. It is a good entry point for the band's core sound of hushed verses breaking into fuzzed-out release.
lineage: Continues the band's Run for Cover run; frequently cited alongside Duster and Bedhead as a reference point for 2020s slowcore revival bands.

label: Run for Cover Records
description: Heartbreak Rules keeps Horse Jumper of Love's slow, weighty tempos while pushing the vocals closer to the front of the mix. It is a moody, unhurried record about heartbreak, delivered with the band's usual dry understatement.
lineage: A steady continuation of the band's Run for Cover-era sound between Natural Part and Disaster Trick.
key_tracks: A Tune Drifts Out the Window

label: Run for Cover Records
description: Disaster Trick was a 2024 favorite Josh Terry left off his year-end list only because he had written the album's press bio; it is another slow, heavy-lidded set of Horse Jumper of Love songs, all murmured vocals and guitars that build toward distorted release.
lineage: The band's most recent full-length, continuing their run for cover as one of the most visible modern slowcore-adjacent groups.
